speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; please tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they occur in other fingers as well.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you. The mechanism of injury sounds like an acute trauma rather than an inflammatory process. Did you hear or feel a "snap" or "pop" at the time of the injury, and is your finger currently crooked or bent differently than the others?

REQUEST TEST: X-ray right hand (AP and lateral views)
REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-rays

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Terminal Extensor Rupture).

The patient's history of forced flexion injury, inability to flex the distal joint, and the extension deformity in the resting position are classic for an avulsion of the extensor tendon. The previous mention of pyelonephritis is clinically unrelated to this upper extremity injury.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
